title: Speed up the complete current P104 native replay by 2.74x
body:
The complete PR6453 native component runs **2.74 times as fast** as the prior gate-table evaluator in three alternating fresh-process pairs on this host: median wall time **24.69 → 9.00 seconds**. Every process reproduces the same 2,941-map recipe receipt and checks all 208 main adapters, helper ranks, signed Pauli images, absolute phases and the wrong-phase rejection.

The new evaluator caches immutable sparse circuit prefixes. The separate native checker uses independent Gray-order action tables. Explicit module forks keep frozen sources intact; there are no source swaps or class patches. AST checks confirm that all other native checks remain. The cache is bounded at 512 entries, and returned lists cannot change cached values.

Evidence: 1,520 complete state comparisons with the original evaluator; 32,768 exact Gray-table entries; circuit, basis, dimension, return-value and eviction controls; complete current-native replay in normal and optimized CPython 3.12. Both registered commands pass. The official 24-file export, committed bytes/modes, and read-only Git-free empty-PATH replays pass. Exported normal/optimized scientific receipts are identical; source corruption is rejected. Input attributes preserve the original CRLF receipt bytes. Full-history checking is unavailable in the shallow checkout; live source pins point to this branch's retained-input ancestors.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-native-prefix-replay`. The package also supplies a fresh-process benchmark command and all six measurements with exact source/input hashes. Timing varies by host; it is not a correctness gate.

Scope: **native verification speed only**, not a full caller/compiler replay, practical multiplier speedup, new kappa or independent scientific acceptance. All five framework assumptions remain. The next step is explicit integration into a complete current candidate and a full caller/compiler replay.

Base and submission refresh: canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19363111). Full overlap coverage: 424 open PRs and 6,380 discussion records, followed by a live submission refresh. PR662 and Wentao Li's PR2329 already provide gate tables; that method is the baseline, and its prior speedup is not reclaimed.

Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. Charles Bethin, Cinna Davis, David Arias, Gareth Davidson, Erwan L., Rohan Arun and the retained native/P104 lineage keep their source and construction credit. All changes are isolated in `research/p104-native-prefix-replay/`; selected-frontier records are unchanged.
